description: Student in the Mechanical and Electrical Engineering program, eager to learn more about the programs offered by NASA.
summary: NASAFARM is a global, single-click agrometeorological decision-support platform built for the "Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data" challenge. Smallholder farmers across climate-vulnerable regions like Jaén, Cajamarca (Peru) face erratic rainfall, heat extremes, and El Niño (ENSO) anomalies without access to local weather stations or actionable satellite intelligence. NASAFARM solves this gap by transforming real-time and 30-year baseline (1991–2020) telemetry from NASA POWER (MERRA-2, CERES, GPM), ISRIC SoilGrids v2.0 (250m soil properties), and Open-Meteo elevation/forecast APIs into localized agronomic prescriptions. With one click on any parcel worldwide, farmers receive deterministic Growing Degree Days (GDD) aligned with MIDAGRI crop thresholds (rice, fruit trees, coffee, pulses, and tubers), phenological harvest estimates, net/gross irrigation depths (ET₀ × Kc), 48-hour phytosanitary risk alerts, safe fertilization windows, and quarterly drought/heat scenarios—democratizing NASA Earthdata into transparent, field-ready climate resilience.
details:
HOW IT WORKS & CORE ARCHITECTURE

NASAFARM operates as a zero-hardware, universal agrometeorological station accessible from any web browser at https://aesthetic-gnome-54cd45.netlify.app/. When a user selects a crop (Grains/Rice, Fruit Trees, Coffee, Legumes/Pulses, or Tubers), sets a sowing date, and clicks any parcel on the interactive global map, the platform automatically retrieves the parcel's coordinates and elevation and executes deterministic agronomic models:

1. Growing Degree Days (GDD) & Phenology Engine: Computes cumulative thermal development using GDD = Σ max(0, (Tmax + Tmin)/2 − Tbase) with crop-specific base temperatures (10°C for rice/coffee, 12°C for fruit trees, 8°C for pulses, 4°C for tubers) aligned with MIDAGRI (Peru) guidelines, tracking progress from germination to harvest.

2. Soil & Elevation Profiling: Queries ISRIC SoilGrids v2.0 (0–5 cm at 250m resolution) to display surface soil pH, organic carbon (g/kg), and textural fractions alongside parcel elevation.

3. Daily & 48-Hour Plot Action Plan:

- Phytosanitary Surveillance: Calculates a 0–100 heuristic vulnerability index combining 7-day relative humidity (40 pts), rainfall (35 pts), and thermal extremes (25 pts) to flag fungal risks (e.g., rice blast, coffee rust).

- Precision Irrigation & Field Windows: Estimates net and gross irrigation depths (ET₀ × Kc minus 80% effective rainfall at 85% efficiency), identifies dry/low-wind windows (rain ≤ 5 mm, wind < 3 m/s) for safe fertilization, and evaluates post-harvest solar drying conditions (ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN ≥ 18 MJ/m²/day, RH < 70%).

4. Multi-Year Climatology & Quarterly Scenarios (2027 Q1–Q4): Benchmarks local monthly rainfall anomalies against 1991–2020 climatology and historical extremes (1997–1998 El Niño and 2010–2011 La Niña), providing empirical P10–P90 rainfall bands and drought/heat frequencies.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES & CREATIVITY

Built with HTML5, CSS3, vanilla JavaScript, Leaflet.js (OpenStreetMap/Esri imagery), and Chart.js, hosted on Netlify. What makes NASAFARM unique is its radical scientific transparency: zero generative AI runs at runtime—every calculation is a deterministic, auditable formula accompanied by a full Parameter Coverage Audit table (showing exact valid NASA POWER days) and explicit field-validation disclaimers.

AI DISCLOSURE

Generative AI assistants (Google Gemini, Netlify AI, and Claude by Anthropic) were used solely during development to assist with web code structuring, English UI translation, and presentation formatting. No AI-generated images, videos, or NASA logos were used.
